items.title_orig: Pearl Jam’s Jeff Ament to share hundreds of unseen photos and reflect on formation of band in new book ‘Since Forever’
items.article_text:
The visual memoir will document the band’s runaway success between 1990 and 1998

Pearl Jam bassist Jeff Ament has announced a new photography book titled Since Forever, featuring more than 250 images from the band’s formative years.

The 9” x 12” hardcover book will bring together Ament’s black-and-white photographs of the people, places and moments that surrounded Pearl Jam’s rise during the 1990s.

Created with his brother, designer Barry Ament, the visual memoir will see the photographs accompanied by the musician’s personal reflections and observations. Most of the images were taken between 1990 and 1998, with Ament saying that 90 per cent of them have never previously been made public.

“If there was a goal, it was mostly to save the failing 30-year-old negatives,” he explained. “It was Barry’s idea to make a book.”

“Historically, my family will often get together by creating some kind of project or job. And in some ways, putting together this book was a job for Barry and me – a reason to hang out.”

The book includes photographs taken backstage, in recording studios and during the journeys between shows, offering Ament’s perspective as both a participant in and observer of the band’s breakthrough.

Ament was a prominent figure in Seattle’s legendary alternative music scene before co-founding Pearl Jam, having previously played alongside guitarist Stone Gossard in Green River and Mother Love Bone.

Following the death of Mother Love Bone frontman Andrew Wood in 1990, Ament and Gossard began working with Mike McCready before recruiting Eddie Vedder and forming the band that would become Pearl Jam.

Their debut album ‘Ten’ arrived in 1991 and became one of the defining records of the grunge era, followed by ‘Vs.’, ‘Vitalogy’, ‘No Code’ and ‘Yield’.

Since Forever is available to pre-order through Pearl Jam’s official website here and will arrive at selected independent bookshops on September 25. Further book events featuring Jeff and Barry will be announced in the coming weeks.

Alongside his music, Ament has long worked as a visual artist and designer, earning two Grammy Awards for Best Recording Package.

Since Forever
Photographs and Text by Jeff Ament

For decades, Pearl Jam founding member and bassist Jeff Ament has photographed the people, places, and moments that inspire him. A few years ago he began working through his archive with his brother, acclaimed designer Barry Ament. Their efforts led to Since Forever, a deeply personal visual journal of creativity, friendship, and life on the road. This 9" x 12" hardcover volume features more than 250 black-and-white photographs, accompanied by wry insights, observations, and personal reflections from Ament.

Drawn largely from previously unreleased images, the collection offers a rare and intimate look at the formative years of Pearl Jam as they evolved from a small group of friends into one of the most influential bands of their generation. From backstage and in the studio to the countless miles between stages, Ament's photographs capture candid moments of creativity, camaraderie, and the enduring relationships that helped sustain the band through its meteoric rise.

At once a visual memoir, and a behind-the-scenes chronicle, the book reveals how relationships, travel, joy, and need contribute to the creative process. Since Forever reveals Ament's unique perspective as both participant and observer of a defining time period in music and American culture.

items.title_orig: Pearl Jam’s Jeff Ament Looks Back With ‘Forever’
items.article_text:
Written by Jonathan Cohen | 
  
  
    July 28, 2026 - 1:00 pm

For more than three decades, Jeff Ament has quietly documented life behind the scenes with a camera. This fall, the Pearl Jam bassist/co-founder will finally open the archive with Since Forever, a 9-by-12-inch hardcover photography book arriving Sept. 25.

In the works for four-plus years, the volume pairs more than 250 black-and-white photographs, most of them previously unpublished, with the musician’s personal reflections, observations and stories from the Rock and Roll Hall of Famers’ formative years. The project began not as a memoir but as a rescue mission, when Ament and his brother, acclaimed designer Barry Ament, started sorting through “something like 300 rolls of” deteriorating film before deciding to shape their discoveries into a something tangible.

“If there was a goal, it was mostly to save the failing 30-year-old negatives. It was Barry’s idea to make a book,” Jeff Ament said. “Historically, my family will often get together by creating some kind of project or job. And in some ways, putting together this book was a job for Barry and me — a reason to hang out. Most of these photos are from 1990 to 1998. He was there for a lot of it. If he wasn’t, he was next door or a phone call away. We [digitized] about 10,000 photos in the process. We also went through my stacks of journals, pulled out some light bulbs, memories [and] pertinent dreams [and] put them in the mix.”

Since Forever traces Pearl Jam’s evolution from the remnants of Seattle rock band Mother Love Bone into one of the defining rock bands of the ‘1990s and beyond. Along the way, Ament captures backstage scenes, recording sessions, endless highway miles and candid moments that illuminate the relationships and creative spirit he’s shared with bandmates Eddie Vedder, Stone Gossard and Mike McCready.

“Ninety percent of these photos have never been seen before,” said Ament, who has long been the Pearl Jam member most willing to both address and revisit the band’s past. “Anybody who’s a PJ fan or a fan of what was going on in the ”90s will dig it.”

The book will be available at select independent bookstores beginning Sept. 25, with preorders open now through Pearl Jam’s web site. Jeff and Barry Ament will also discuss Since Forever during appearances on the Storytellers Stage at Vedder’s Ohana Festival on Sept. 25 and 27 in Dana Point, Ca., with additional book events in select cities to be announced in the coming weeks.

Although best known for his work in Pearl Jam, Ament has long pursued creative work beyond music, from solo albums and film scores to Grammy-winning visual design and decades of skatepark advocacy throughout Montana and the American West. Barry Ament, meanwhile, has spent more than 30 years as co-founder of Seattle design studio Ames Bros, creating artwork for Pearl Jam that spans album packaging, merchandise and more than 500 concert posters.

As previously reported, Pearl Jam is returning to live duty at Ohana for the first time since May 18, 2025. It will also be the band’s first show with an as-yet-unnamed new drummer, following longtime member Matt Cameron’s departure last summer. McCready also has a book coming out of sorts this fall, in the form of the graphic novel Farewell to Seasons.
